title: Дыхательная гимнастика Вики  (Vika's Prenatal Breathing Class)

segments.t: Season five opens at a prenatal class, where Vika is practicing breathing exercises before suddenly realizing she is only five months pregnant and becoming absent-minded. Listen to the Russian conversation first, and then we will unpack every line.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Strong contractions.' The doctor frames one key expression on cue: "skhvatki" means "contractions" (from "skhvatka"), giving the line its exact edge.
'I am with you.' Kostya makes that thought on cue: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'My butterfly.' Kostya follows up quietly in this moment, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'Take more air in.' The doctor focuses on one key expression in reply: "vozdukh" means "air", and it carries the main weight of what the doctor is saying.
'Come on, everything is fine.' Kostya aims the thought frankly here: starting with "davay" is the classic everyday Russian way to say "come on, let's do this" between people on close terms.
'We are almost there already.' The doctor continues warmly watching Vika, leaving no doubt about where he stands.
'Come on, let's breathe.' The doctor leans on one memorable element right here: "dyshim" means "to breathe" (from "dyshat"), giving the line its exact edge.

'Do you have a conscience?' Vika frames this update facing Kostya: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Kostya purely through rising pitch at the end.
'The baby is only five months along.' Vika speaks up warmly to settle things, letting the remark speak for itself.
'What is with you, mommy, huh?' The doctor uses this vivid detail toward Vika: "mamochka" means "mommy", and it carries the main weight of what the doctor is saying.
'We have become completely absent-minded.' Vika frames this answer without fuss: adding "sovsem" ("completely, at all") pushes the statement all the way, leaving zero room for doubt.
'Oh my God.' Vika proceeds candidly without any doubt, so Kostya knows she is not just making small talk.
And that brings Vika's prenatal class mix-up to a close. Until next time!
